org_hagg_taurenbane.description:
There's a champion up on that ridge, and I need him dead before he becomes a story. His name's Hagg Taurenbane, and he's earned it the hard way. Ask any patrol that's crossed him and lived, and there are fewer of those than I'd like.

Here's the urgent part, and it isn't the killing. Single warbands have stopped patrolling that stretch altogether. Nobody gave the order. They just stopped, one at a time, and nobody reported it. I only noticed from the duty rosters. He's taken a mile of ground off us without leaving his ridge.

Kill him before the Razormane rally round the idea of him. Once a tribe decides a man can't be killed, killing him stops being enough. You have to do it in front of them, and that's a much harder afternoon.
org_hagg_taurenbane.turn_in_text:
He bled like anything else does.

The stories will outlive him, because they always do, but at least they're only stories now, and the patrols will go back out.

org_into_the_broodspiral.description:
I'm Apothecary Zurm. Mind the step, and ignore the smell, because it's the work and not the room.

I've become worried about what's at the centre of that tunnel network, and it isn't the silithid. We've dealt with nests before. It's the spiral. A nest spreads where the digging is easy, it branches and wanders, and that's what makes them survivable. This one goes down in a spiral, which means it's heading somewhere specific, and something decided where.

So I want it confirmed properly, not rumoured about by dockhands. Clear the Silithid Guardians off the outer tunnels, and then we'll know whether this deserves Orgrimmar's real attention, which is a sentence I've avoided writing for a month.
org_into_the_broodspiral.turn_in_text:
The tunnels go deeper than that. Whatever's at the centre of that spiral, it hasn't finished growing.

I've written that down, and I don't like seeing it in my own handwriting.

org_quilboar_territories.accept_text: Look for banners or totems on the high ground. A position always marks itself.

org_razormane_incursion.description:
The ridge is confirmed, so now we bleed it, and I'll be straight about the goal. It isn't conquest and it never was. I want the Razormane to think again about testing us.

I'm not taking that ridge. I haven't got the men, and I couldn't hold it if I had. What I want is for the next quilboar who suggests pushing toward the southern trade routes to get an argument from somebody in his own camp, and that only happens if this raid costs them. A small raid they shrug off. A real one gets talked about round their own fire.

The Razormane Stalkers work Blackthorn Ridge, north of Razorfen Kraul. Kill as many as you can, as obviously as you can.
org_razormane_incursion.accept_text: Leave the bodies where the others will find them. That's what gets talked about round the fire.
org_razormane_incursion.turn_in_text:
The ridge won't forget this raid, and they'll think twice next time.

I couldn't make that happen with a warband, and you've done it in an afternoon.

org_snizzles_curiosity.description:
I'm Snizzle Boltcrank. Don't touch anything on that bench. Most of it's mid-experiment, and one of them's mid-argument.

There's a brand-new silithid tunnel network south-east of Ratchet. I want to dwell on the word new, because everybody skips past it. Silithid nests are old. You find one, and it turns out it's been there since before anybody local had a word for it. I've never in my career heard of one appearing, and this one did. So something's changed, recently, in a creature that doesn't change, and I'd very much like to know what.

I want hardened chitin off the silithid in those tunnels, the kind that comes off something that's had to fight for its life. A creature that's had to armour itself was expecting something.
org_snizzles_curiosity.accept_text: Bring the pieces with scratches on them. I want to know what they were fighting.
org_snizzles_curiosity.turn_in_text:
That's a fascinating structure. Look at the layering. That isn't growth, it's a response.

This will keep me busy for weeks. I'm grateful, genuinely, and I don't say that often at this bench.

org_the_broodkeeper.description:
The outer tunnels are confirmed dangerous, which I expected, and organised, which I didn't. There's a Broodkeeper deeper in the Broodspiral, south-east of Ratchet, a caster of sorts, tending the egg chambers.

Tending is the word I keep coming back to, and it's why I'm sending you instead of writing another report. Silithid don't tend. They lay and they leave, and the hive works or it doesn't. Every text I own agrees on that. Something down below is looking after eggs on purpose, and the growth we've measured is exactly what you'd expect if it were.

Every day it lives, the hive grows faster. Kill it and buy the surface some real time. That's all I'm promising, because the eggs are already laid.
org_the_broodkeeper.accept_text: Burn the egg chambers on your way out if you can. Killing it buys time, and fire buys more.
org_the_broodkeeper.turn_in_text:
The egg chambers have gone quiet, for now.

They won't stay that way forever, but they'll stay that way long enough, which is the only promise anyone in my trade gets to make.

org_the_queens_silence.description:
I've confirmed what I feared, and I'll say it plainly instead of hedging it the way I've been hedging it for a fortnight. Something massive rules the centre of that spiral. It's a Queen, and everything down there answers to her, which is what turns a nest into a problem.

An unorganised hive is a hazard. It eats what's near it and grows where the ground allows, and you can live beside one for a generation. An organised one decides. I've watched this one dig a spiral toward something, tend its own eggs, and armour its workers against a threat it was expecting, and I don't know what it's expecting.

Kill her, and the hive loses its reason to keep growing. This is the real fight. Everything before it was the approach.
org_the_queens_silence.turn_in_text:
The Broodspiral is silent now.

It won't stay empty, because nothing in the Barrens ever does. But for now it's quiet, and you did something genuinely difficult down there. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise, because somebody will try.

ratchet_brontus.description:
This one's half business, and I'll tell you which half. Every sailor who's been inland has a story about a kodo called Brontus, and I've been collecting them for six years without meaning to.

He's ancient, and the stories all agree he's elite, and sailors agree on nothing. He's old enough to have a reputation that reached this port before I did. Half the stories are probably true, which is a generous estimate. The trouble is which half, because the dangerous half is real either way. He roams Blackthorn Ridge, and my drivers go round it, and going round costs me.

So hunt him, and bring back proof, and I'll believe the rest of it. Then I'll tell the story myself, badly, for years.
ratchet_brontus.accept_text: Bring me a horn if you can. The drivers won't believe anything less.
ratchet_brontus.turn_in_text:
You actually did it!

I'll be telling this story myself now, and I'll be getting it wrong within a fortnight. You've earned this.

ratchet_raptor_hides.description:
I'm Fishmonger Gribble. Yes, I know what the stall says, but hear me out. I've got a side trade in raptor hide.

Fish is the business. Fish is reliable and boring, and it's kept this stall open through two bad years. Raptor hide is the margin, and the Sunscale raptors are the closest real supply on this coast. Everything else comes up from the south at a price that eats the point of it.

The Sunscale screechers hunt thickest along the Southfury banks, north of here, and the lashtails keep to the Raptor Grounds in the Southern Barrens. Bring the hides back as whole as you can manage. That isn't fussiness. A hide with a hole through the middle is worth about a third, because the buyers cut panels, and a panel has to be clean.
ratchet_raptor_hides.accept_text: Skin them along the belly. A cut down the back ruins the best panel.
ratchet_raptor_hides.turn_in_text:
That's good hide, and barely torn.

This will fetch a real price at the docks, and I won't be telling anyone where it came from.

ratchet_thinning_the_grounds.description:
I'm Kala, and I hunt for the camp. Walk with me a moment.

The kodo moved south early this year, and I've been finding out why. It's the raptors. The Sunscale on the Raptor Grounds have bred past what the ground can feed, and the lashtails, the young bold hunters, have started running the herds instead of the strays. A herd that's run doesn't graze, and a herd that doesn't graze doesn't calve. I won't have this camp go hungry in spring for the sake of a raptor's good year.

Thin the Sunscale Lashtails on the Raptor Grounds, south through Camp Taurajo on the east side of the Southern Barrens. Don't kill them all, because the Grounds are theirs. Kill only enough that they remember it.
ratchet_thinning_the_grounds.accept_text: Leave the nesting females be. The Grounds need the next generation, just a smaller one.
ratchet_thinning_the_grounds.turn_in_text:
That's enough, so leave the rest.

The herds will come back up by the next moon. I don't think you'll see it, because you have the look of someone going south. But the calves will, and they're who it was for.

ratchet_zulrakas_toll.description:
I'm Zulraka, a dockhand, which means I walk, mon, more than anybody here realises.

There's a silithid dig south-east of this port, spiralling down into the earth, and I've heard it's been growing. I'm not a scholar, and I've no business having a theory about bugs. Here's my business. I walk the coast road every week, the same stretch, and when you walk a road for years, you learn what it sounds like under your feet. It's been different past the fourth mile since spring. It sounds hollow.

If that dig keeps going, it undermines the road, and one week it won't be a road and I'll be on it. Go and look, and tell me how deep it goes.
ratchet_zulrakas_toll.accept_text: Stamp as you walk past the fourth mile. You'll hear what I mean, mon.
ratchet_zulrakas_toll.turn_in_text:
It's deeper than I hoped and not as deep as I feared.

Thank you for checking, mon. I'll sleep easier walking that road, though I'll still walk on the inland side of it.

taurajo_beastcallers_request.description:
I'm Beastcaller Nira. Speak quietly, there's one sleeping.

I want Sunscale eggs from the Raptor Grounds east of here, off the lashtails that guard them, and unbroken if you can manage it. I think I can hatch one. Taming a caught raptor has been done, and it's a miserable business for everyone, and the animal never stops knowing. I want to hatch one and have it know me before it knows anything else.

I've been working toward it for six years. I've had two eggs in that time and lost both, one to a crack I didn't see and one to my own impatience. So be careful. Unbroken means unbroken, because a hairline crack is a dead raptor a few weeks later.
taurajo_beastcallers_request.accept_text: Wrap each egg in grass and carry them against your body. They need the warmth.
taurajo_beastcallers_request.turn_in_text:
They're still warm!

This might actually work. I won't say more than that, because I've said more than that before. Thank you, truly. This is rare work.

taurajo_dwarven_excavation.description:
The keep's confirmed, so now for the dig itself. I'd like to put a number on what's really bothering me, because it isn't the hole.

That excavation has spread further into tauren-claimed ground every single season I've watched it. It's a little each time, never enough to be worth a complaint, and that's exactly the method, whether or not anyone down there thinks of it as one. I drove kodo past the boundary stone for twenty years. It's now a long way inside their workings, and nobody ever crossed a line, because the line moved under it a yard at a time.

So I want the crews thinned. Kill the Dwarf Miners and give me one season where the stone stays where it is.
taurajo_dwarven_excavation.turn_in_text:
That'll slow their digging by a season, at least.

I'll go and look at the boundary stone this week. It's the first time in three years I'll be able to stand at it.

taurajo_general_twinbraids_folly.description:
I've watched General Twinbraid grow bolder with every site he claims, and I want to be exact about why I'm asking, because this will look like vengeance, and it isn't. I've no quarrel with dwarves. I've traded with them, and I knew one well, years back. I'd have called him a friend if either of us had used the word.

Twinbraid doesn't really dig for ore any more. He digs for territory and calls it prospecting, and the name matters, because a man who's found a word for what he's doing has stopped hearing anyone tell him not to. He doesn't respect any boundary at all now, not ours and not his own Keep's.

Someone needs to remind him where Bael'dun's walls end. I'd have preferred that to be a conversation, and it was, twice.
taurajo_general_twinbraids_folly.turn_in_text:
Twinbraid's dead, and the digging stops for a while.

It'll start again eventually, because somebody else will have the same idea and a better word for it. But this has bought the land some peace, and peace always has to be bought.

taurajo_spiritcarvers_balance.description:
Sit with me. I've been needing somebody who's actually seen it rather than heard about it. I'm Spiritcarver Dennok.

I want to lay this out in order, because the order is what worries me. There's quilboar fighting quilboar to the north, which has gone on for generations. There are dwarves digging where they shouldn't to the south, for three or four years now, and faster all the time. And something ancient is waking in the earth beneath both of them. Any one of those is a season's problem. All three at once, in one lifetime, on one plain, isn't three problems. It's one thing happening, and I can't see its shape.

So tell me what you saw, all of it, in your own order. I need to think this through with somebody whose hands were in it.
taurajo_spiritcarvers_balance.accept_text: Start wherever it began for you. The order you tell it in might be the shape I'm missing.
taurajo_spiritcarvers_balance.turn_in_text:
You've given me a clearer picture than I had, and a worse one. Whatever comes of it, at least I'm not guessing any more.

Come back if you see more, and you will.

taurajo_word_from_bael_modan.description:
The dwarves have been digging at Bael Modan for years, and nobody here has minded very much. I want to be fair about that. They put a hole in some ground nobody was grazing, and for a long while that was the whole story.

Word now is they've built a proper fortress over it, Bael'dun Keep, and that's a different thing. You don't build a keep over a hole unless you mean to be at the bottom of it for a very long time, or unless you expect somebody to come and stop you.

I'm meant to be watching the centaur, so go south to Bael Modan and look at the keep for me before Camp Taurajo turns its attention south. I'd rather look foolish for asking than find out from a dwarf.
taurajo_word_from_bael_modan.accept_text: Count the chimneys on the keep. Dwarves don't light a forge for a short stay.
